subject: SparkBridge integration fit checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira@sparkbridge.ai>, Amit Rao <devops@sparkbridge.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: SparkBridge integration fit checklist & next steps

Hi Samira / Amit,

Thanks for taking the time today — good conversation. I wanted to capture the agreed pain points, the product fit signals we saw, and a short mutual action plan so we have alignment going into a PoC. Attaching the action plan and the call recording.

TLDR pain points we heard
- Latency spikes on live customer transcripts at 8k+ tokens causing timeouts in their routing layer
- Ranking relevance for multi-turn search is brittle; they lose key entity context across turns
- Heavy cost from naive per-request full-context inference for reranking and summaries

Goals SparkBridge stated
1) Replace current reranker with an embeddings+rerank flow that preserves entity context across sessions
2) Add streaming decode with early partial responses for the live transcript UI to reduce perceived latency
3) Keep 95th percentile latency for the transcript path under 350ms and reduce inference cost by at least 30% vs today

Product fit and technical notes from call
- SDK: They will need a small client-side integration to support streaming + function calling; prefer a single endpoint that can stream tokens and structured JSON metadata (entities, timestamps).
- Function calling: There are two canonical tool hooks they want: a) entity normalization service, b) routing decision API for escalation. These should be callable via the same session so KV cache persists.
- Streaming: We proposed our streaming+partial-output pattern with fallback to batch inference for long docs; showed benchmarks for 4k/8k contexts.
- Structured outputs: They emphasized a strict JSON schema for the reranker and summary outputs (example in sample-output.json).
- Embeddings/rerank: Their current pipeline uses off-the-shelf vectors per chunk; suggested approach is session-level embedding + incremental reranking using partial KV cache to preserve entity context.

Mutual action plan (owners + target dates)
1) Share SDK integration checklist and sample structured output schema — Ben (this thread), by Mon 2027-04-05 (attached sample-output.json).
2) PoC scope doc with success metrics (latency, cost delta, relevance lift) — SparkBridge product team (Samira) by Wed 2027-04-07.
3) Demo environment and API keys for PoC (sandbox cluster) — Amit (SparkBridge) by Fri 2027-04-09.
4) Redwood to provide streaming + function-calling PoC template and quickstart scripts — Karthik by Mon 2027-04-12.
5) Pricing proposal and 30-day pilot discount terms — Ben / Sales by Tue 2027-04-13.

Open questions we flagged
- Do you need encrypted request logs or full-audit for transcript retention? If yes, we should scope Private deployment or VPC options.
- Expected QPS for the transcript path at peak? We need that to size batching and instance types.

Next steps
- Samira to confirm PoC scope and peak QPS.
- We will send the SDK checklist and a preliminary mu-action plan spreadsheet (attached).

Thanks again, looking forward to partnering on this.

Best,
Ben Carter

Thanks Ben — great summary and much appreciated. A few clarifications from our side:
- For PoC success metrics, add 'entity recall for support cases' with baseline 0.62; target 0.80.
- We will need the structured output JSON to include an external_case_id field so our downstream systems can reconcile.
- We expect peak QPS of ~65 for the live transcript route during support surges.

We can commit to the PoC scope doc by 2027-04-07. On the pilot discount, can Redwood provide a 30-day pilot at 50% list pricing for the inference layer? That would make budget sign-off easier.

I also turned on recording for the demo and uploaded it to our shared drive, link included below.

Thanks — Samira

Looping you both in — forwarding Samira's confirmation and the action plan. Key asks: streaming tokens with structured JSON metadata, function-call hooks for routing + normalization, and a session-level embedding strategy for rerank. They expect peak QPS ~65 and want a 30-day pilot.

Internal notes / recommended approach
- Recommend we run the PoC on a 2-node dedicated GPU pool with aggressive batching and prefix KV caching; this should hit their 350ms p95 with the streaming fallback enabled.
- SDK change: provide a single streaming client that multiplexes token stream and JSON event frames. We'll need a small client-side shim for their web UI. Karthik, please confirm estimated engineering time for the shim and quickstart.
- Pricing: I think a 50% pilot discount for 30 days is acceptable but prefer to propose 40% and leave room to sign a 6-12 month committed Dedicated contract if PoC metrics are hit.

Can you both confirm feasibility and rough effort estimates? I want to have a proposed PoC quote ready by Tue 2027-04-13.
